papers.title: Proliferation of Osteoblasts on Laser-Modified Nanostructured Titanium Surfaces.
papers.abstract: Nanostructured titanium has become a useful material for biomedical applications such as dental implants. Certain surface properties (grain size, roughness, wettability) are highly expected to promote cell adhesion and osseointegration. The aim of this study was to compare the biocompatibilities of several titanium materials using human osteoblast cell line hFOB 1.19. Eight different types of specimens were examined: machined commercially pure grade 2 (cpTi2) and 4 (cpTi4) titanium, nanostructured titanium of the same grades (nTi2, nTi4), and corresponding specimens with laser-treated surfaces (cpTi2L, cpTi4L, nTi2L, nTi4L). Their surface topography was evaluated by means of scanning electron microscopy. Surface roughness was measured using a mechanical contact profilometer. Specimens with laser-treated surfaces had significantly higher surface roughness. Wettability was measured by the drop contact angle method. Nanostructured samples had significantly higher wettability. Cell proliferation after 48 hours from plating was assessed by viability and proliferation assay. The highest proliferation of osteoblasts was found in nTi4 specimens. The analysis of cell proliferation revealed a difference between machined and laser-treated specimens. The mean proliferation was lower on the laser-treated titanium materials. Although plain laser treatment increases surface roughness and wettability, it does not seem to lead to improved biocompatibility.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了钛表面改性对成骨细胞增殖的影响，但未涉及LPBF增材制造、多孔结构或疲劳性能，与用户研究方向间接相关。
llm.why_not_core: No LPBF fabrication, no porous structure for stress shielding, no fatigue testing, no osseointegration in vivo.

summary_zh.motivation: 比较不同钛材料表面处理后的生物相容性。
summary_zh.method: 使用人成骨细胞系评估机械加工、纳米结构和激光处理钛表面的细胞增殖。
summary_zh.result: 激光处理增加了粗糙度和润湿性但未提高生物相容性，纳米Ti4增殖最高。
summary_zh.validation: 体外细胞活力和增殖实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: To compare the biocompatibility of titanium materials with different surface modifications for dental implant applications.
summary_en.method: Human osteoblast cell line hFOB 1.19 was cultured on machined, nanostructured, and laser-treated cpTi2, cpTi4 surfaces; cell proliferation was measured after 48 hours.
summary_en.result: Laser treatment increased surface roughness and wettability but did not enhance osteoblast proliferation; nanostructured Ti4 exhibited the highest proliferation among all groups.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell viability and proliferation assay using hFOB 1.19 osteoblasts.

papers.title: 3D Printed Stem-Cell Derived Neural Progenitors Generate Spinal Cord Scaffolds.
papers.abstract: A bioengineered spinal cord is fabricated via extrusion-based multi-material 3D bioprinting, in which clusters of induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived spinal neuronal progenitor cells (sNPCs) and oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs) are placed in precise positions within 3D printed biocompatible scaffolds during assembly. The location of a cluster of cells, of a single type or multiple types, is controlled using a point-dispensing printing method with a 200 μm center-to-center spacing within 150 μm wide channels. The bioprinted sNPCs differentiate and extend axons throughout microscale scaffold channels, and the activity of these neuronal networks is confirmed by physiological spontaneous calcium flux studies. Successful bioprinting of OPCs in combination with sNPCs demonstrates a multicellular neural tissue engineering approach, where the ability to direct the patterning and combination of transplanted neuronal and glial cells can be beneficial in rebuilding functional axonal connections across areas of central nervous system (CNS) tissue damage. This platform can be used to prepare novel biomimetic, hydrogel-based scaffolds modeling complex CNS tissue architecture in vitro and harnessed to develop new clinical approaches to treat neurological diseases, including spinal cord injury.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文专注于3D生物打印脊髓支架，未涉及任何人工智能或机器学习方法。
llm.why_not_core: This paper lacks any AI/ML integration, computational modeling, or autonomous decision-making; it is purely experimental bioprinting.

summary_zh.motivation: 构建生物工程化的脊髓支架以修复中枢神经损伤。
summary_zh.method: 采用挤出式多材料3D生物打印，将iPSC来源的神经前体细胞精确放置于支架内。
summary_zh.result: 打印的细胞分化并延伸轴突，通过钙流实验验证了神经元活性。
summary_zh.validation: 体外细胞实验，包括免疫染色和钙成像。

summary_en.motivation: To fabricate bioengineered spinal cord scaffolds for repairing central nervous system damage.
summary_en.method: Extrusion-based multi-material 3D bioprinting was used to precisely position iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells within hydrogel scaffolds.
summary_en.result: Bioprinted cells differentiated, extended axons, and exhibited spontaneous calcium activity.
summary_en.validation: In vitro validation through immunostaining and calcium imaging.
